facts.Page story text 1 (draft, teacher check: Mowgli was different from the wolves he lived with. He had no fur and he walked on two legs. He could not howl at the moon like the rest. But the pack accepted him because he kept their Law. He respected the same elders and guarded the same land. Shared rules make very different creatures into one family. Law creates belonging.
facts.Page story text 2 (draft, teacher check: Mowgli had always been different from the wolves he lived with in the pack. He had no fur and he ran on two legs and he could not howl properly at the moon. But the wolf pack had accepted him completely because he lived by their shared Law. He obeyed the same rules and respected the same elders and protected the same territory. The Law did not ask that all animals be the same — only that they share the same standards. Because Mowgli honored the Law he was truly a member of the pack in every way that mattered. Shared rules are what turn a group of individuals into something that can be called a community. Law creates belonging.
facts.Page story text 3 (draft, teacher check: By any reasonable measure, Mowgli should not have belonged among the wolves of the Seeonee pack at all. He had no fur, he ran awkwardly on two legs, and his attempts to howl at the moon had always embarrassed the entire pack. Yet the wolves had accepted him completely, and not a single member of the pack ever treated him as an outsider. The reason for this acceptance had nothing to do with his appearance or his skills or his natural abilities as a hunter. It had to do with the fact that Mowgli lived by the same Law that every other member of the pack lived by. He respected the same elders, protected the same territory, observed the same rituals, and kept the same promises. The Law, Mowgli slowly came to understand, did not require uniformity — it required only shared commitment to a common set of standards. A boy who kept the Law was more truly a wolf than a wolf who broke it could ever hope to be. Law creates belonging.
